A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GAR and GAR-Bench. All 27 pages of v1 and 29 pages of v3, including equations, tables, figures and appendices, support comparison. Renumbered and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original GAR evaluations on image and video benchmarks, architectural and training-data ablations, and qualitative results in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds architectural controls, general-data mixing, subsampling, cross-judge validation and input-format experiments.

M1.justification: The proposed mask embedding, AnyRes image encoding, RoI-aligned feature replay and supervised fine-tuning procedure remain unchanged. The additional architectural rows are ablation controls, and the general-data experiment changes training coverage rather than introducing a new algorithm or objective.

E1.justification: Table 11 adds an evaluated GAR-8B variant trained with 600K general-VQA examples attributed to Li et al. (2024), extending training beyond the original region-focused data. The existing image and video evaluation benchmarks and their task coverage are retained.

E2.justification: v3 removes GPT4RoI-7B from the DLC-Bench comparison in Table 3, adds Shikra-7B to the LVIS/PACO comparison in Table 5, and adds the unfine-tuned PerceptionLM-8B comparator in Table 11. Most external comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix C adds substantial evaluation protocols: per-subtask 50% and 25% subsampling, three additional captioning judges, four region-specification formats, and a general-data training control. Existing main protocols remain intact. The new captioning subsampling table reports 214 full-set examples, inconsistent with 204 in Table 2.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's existing ablations and failure cases, v3 adds four architectural controls examining mask encoding, pooling and global/local features in Table 8. Tables 11-15 additionally examine general-data mixing, benchmark sampling stability, judge sensitivity and region-input formats, substantially broadening validation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new subsampling comparisons report point scores and ranks, without repeated-resampling information or a statistical uncertainty estimate.

E6.justification: Previously reported GAR scores are retained, but Tables 8 and 11-15 add substantial quantitative findings. The new general-data variant scores 51.6 on MMStar versus the retained GAR-8B score of 43.9, under different training conditions. Cross-judge results newly show GAR-8B ranked first under all four judges.

T1.justification: The task definition and Equation 1 are unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs, and the added empirical analyses introduce no new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: contextual region understanding through feature replay, multi-prompt reasoning, GAR-Bench and image-to-video transfer. The headline comparisons against DAM-3B, InternVL3-78B and VideoRefer-7B are unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 newly interprets subsampling and cross-judge results as supporting ranking stability and resistance to judge bias. It attributes general models' difficulties across input formats to deficient fine-grained perception and relational reasoning, and discusses general-VQA data mixing. Existing temporal-motion and complex-relation limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix C and Figure 7 newly document general-model region-input formats, including the original separated global/local input setting; Table 11 identifies the additional data source and size. v3 omits v1's direct GAR-1B checkpoint link while retaining the repository link. Core optimizer settings and data-generation prompt templates are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds references including Lee et al. (2024), Groma and three diffusion-model papers. It replaces the blanket statement that previous approaches support only one prompt with a more specific contrast between global-context preservation and local-detail retention. The overall research positioning remains recognizable.

P1.justification: The introduction and related-work motivation receive localized rewrites, Appendix C gains explanatory passages, and author information and acknowledgements change. Citations switch to author-year style. The main section sequence and Appendix A-H organization remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: The document is reformatted from the branded layout and boxed abstract to the ICLR template, with extensive table reflow and relocation. Tables 8 and 11 expand, four new result tables and an input-format figure are added, and retained figures are renumbered. Existing qualitative examples are preserved.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens v1's empirical support through additional architectural controls, cross-judge checks and input-format analyses. The base-model comparison also exposes general-task tradeoffs and partial recovery through data mixing. These benefits are limited by missing uncertainty estimates and experimental details, overstated stability language, and inconsistent captioning sample counts between Tables 2 and 13.
